pages.text: Long before cities and roads, the first people lived close to nature under wide open skies.
They did not have houses like ours. Some families stayed in caves or built simple shelters from branches.
To find food, they gathered fruits, nuts, and roots from the land.
Sometimes they worked together to hunt animals for meat and clothing.
They shaped sharp stones into tools. Stone tools helped them cut, dig, and build.
One of the biggest discoveries was fire. Fire gave warmth and light at night.
Fire also helped cook food, making it easier to chew and digest.
Over time, people learned new skills and passed knowledge to children.
These early humans slowly traveled across continents, spreading to many parts of the world.
From simple shelters and stone tools, human history began its long journey.
